prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Only a dad, with a tired face, Coming home from the daily race, Bringing little of gold or fame, To show how well he has played the game, But glad in his heart that his own rejoice To see him come, and to hear his voice. Only a dad, with a brood of four, One of ten million men or more. Plodding along in the daily strife, Bearing the whips and the scorns of life, With never a whimper of pain or hate, For the sake of those who at home await. Only a dad, neither rich nor proud, Merely one of the surging crowdToiling, striving from day to day, Facing whatever may come his way, Silent, whenever the harsh condemn, And bearing it all for the love of them. Only a dad, but he gives his allTo smooth the way for his children small, Doing, with courage stern and grim, The deeds that his father did for him. This is the line that for him I pen, Only a dad, but the best of men.

outputs.L2:
Just a father, his face worn with weariness,  
returning home after the day’s long struggle,  
with little wealth or public honor to prove  
how faithfully he has lived his part.  
Yet his heart is happy because his family delights  
in his arrival and in the sound of his voice.

Just a father, with four children of his own,  
one among countless millions of other men,  
moving steadily through life’s daily hardships,  
enduring its insults, burdens, and blows,  
without complaint, bitterness, or anger,  
because loved ones are waiting for him at home.

Just a father, not wealthy and not boastful,  
simply another person in the restless crowd,  
working and struggling from one day to the next,  
meeting whatever troubles come before him,  
staying quiet when others judge him harshly,  
and accepting it all out of love for his family.

Just a father, yet he offers everything he has  
to make life easier for his young children,  
carrying out, with firm and solemn courage,  
the same sacrifices his own father once made for him.  
These are the words I write in his honor:  
only a father, but among the finest of men.
outputs.L3:
The father returns home each day weary from the demands of his work. He may not bring with him great wealth, public honor, or fame, yet his arrival is met with joy. To the family waiting for him, he is far more important than any celebrated man. His presence brings comfort, security, and happiness to the home.

He is an ordinary man among many, living a simple life and facing the hardships that come with it. Day after day, he bears his responsibilities without complaint. Whatever difficulties he encounters, he endures them quietly because he knows that his loved ones depend on him. The thought of those waiting at home gives him strength.

Despite the challenges he faces, he continues to work faithfully and silently. He does not seek praise or recognition for his efforts. Instead, he is motivated by love—love for his family, for his children, and for the life he hopes to provide for them. This love gives meaning to his labor and courage to his struggles.

He gives all that he has to make life easier and better for his children. His sacrifices may often go unnoticed, but they shape the comfort, opportunities, and happiness of those he loves. He puts their needs before his own and finds joy in seeing them safe and content.

Though he may be described as “only a dad,” he is, in truth, one of the best of men. His greatness lies not in fame or fortune, but in devotion, sacrifice, patience, and love. In the eyes of his family, he is deeply honored, and his quiet strength makes him worthy of the highest respect.
outputs.L4:
The poem presents a moving picture of an ordinary father whose life is humble, difficult, and often unnoticed. He is not described as a rich or famous man, nor as someone who receives public praise or recognition. Instead, he is shown as a tired, hard-working figure who gives his strength to his family day after day. His hands, body, and spirit carry the marks of labor, suggesting that his life has been shaped by responsibility and sacrifice. Through this portrayal, the poem asks the reader to recognize the quiet greatness found in a father’s everyday efforts.

A key feature of the poem is its admiring and repetitive praise. By repeatedly emphasizing the father’s goodness, patience, and dedication, the speaker creates a tone of deep respect and affection. This repetition reflects the constancy of the father’s work: just as the poem returns again and again to praise him, the father returns each day to his duties. He provides, protects, and endures, not for applause, but because of his love for his family. His heroism is not dramatic or public; it is expressed through simple acts of care, steady labor, and silent perseverance.

The father’s weariness is especially important because it shows the cost of his devotion. He may have little money, comfort, or social status, but he continues to give what he can. His sacrifices are ordinary, yet they are also deeply meaningful. The poem suggests that true worth should not be measured by wealth, fame, or outward success. Instead, it should be measured by loyalty, kindness, responsibility, and love.

By the end of the poem, the father is praised as “the best of men.” This conclusion gives dignity to his modest life and transforms him into a kind of everyday hero. Although the world may overlook him, the speaker recognizes the greatness of his character. The poem ultimately celebrates the dignity of fatherhood, showing that a man who works tirelessly and lovingly for his family possesses a quiet nobility greater than material achievement or public honor.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a sentimental poem about an ordinary father who works hard every day for his children.
counterfactuals.output:
**An Ordinary Father**

He rises while the house still dreams,  
before the morning stirs,  
and ties his shoes in quiet dark,  
not waking her or hers.  

His coffee cools beside his hand,  
his lunch is packed with care,  
he carries bills and bedtime hopes  
through the early, heavy air.  

He is not praised by marching bands,  
no headlines speak his name,  
but every day he lifts the world  
and shoulders it the same.  

His hands are worn, his back is tired,  
his shirt is stained with years,  
but he still smiles at tiny voices  
and wipes away their tears.  

He counts the hours, saves the change,  
puts dreams upon a shelf,  
so his children might have more  
than he ever had himself.  

At night, he comes home quietly,  
with aching feet and grace,  
and all the love he never says  
is written on his face.  

An ordinary father, yes—  
but only to the eye.  
To those he loves, he is the roof,  
the roots, the steady sky.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Give me a Father’s Day poem honoring a humble dad who sacrifices for his family.
counterfactuals.output:
For every quiet sacrifice  
You’ve made without applause,  
For steady hands, a patient heart,  
And love that never paused—  

For early mornings, long days too,  
And dreams you set aside,  
So we could have a better path,  
With you there as our guide—  

You never asked for praise or thanks,  
You simply gave your best,  
A humble strength, a faithful love,  
A heart that would not rest.  

Today we honor who you are,  
The good man we’ve always had—  
With grateful hearts, we celebrate  
Our loving, selfless dad.

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose a traditional rhyming poem in the style of Edgar Guest about a hardworking father.
counterfactuals.output:
He rises when the dawn is gray,  
Before the robins start to sing,  
And quietly he goes his way  
To face the labor day will bring.  
His coat is old, his hands are worn,  
His boots are stained with dust and rain;  
Yet every new and misty morn  
He shoulders hope and hides his pain.  

He never asks for much in life,  
A chair, a meal, a little rest,  
The laughter of his kids and wife,  
And knowing he has done his best.  
He mends the gate, he pays the due,  
He saves a dime when times are lean;  
And if the sky is gray or blue,  
He keeps the home fires bright and clean.  

The world may praise the men of fame,  
The mighty ones who lead the crowd,  
But there is glory in the name  
Of father, humble, brave, and proud.  
For he who toils from sun to sun,  
With love behind each weary stride,  
Has built a kingdom, one by one,  
Where hearts are warm and doors are wide.  

So here’s to him whose strength is plain,  
Whose dreams are often set aside;  
Who smiles through worry, loss, and strain,  
And makes his children’s road more wide.  
No monument of bronze or stone  
Could speak the worth his days impart;  
His truest honor stands alone—  
A family sheltered by his heart.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
